underlying_release: libpg_query 18.0.0 (linked statically into pg_query.so), source-built for both the coverage image and the AFL++ overlay
coverage_limit: One run records Clang/LLVM source coverage of the pg_query extension (ext/pg_query.c) and of source-built libpg_query 18.0.0 (PostgreSQL raw parser, memory contexts and JSON output functions) linked into pg_query.so, for one pg_query_parse() call on a valid control. PHP itself is a plain build and is not covered; the JSON decode and summary walk in summary.php run no extension or libpg_query code. AFL++ feedback comes from the native overlay: ext/pg_query.c plus libpg_query src_backend_parser_gram.c, src_backend_parser_scan.c and src_backend_parser_parser.c, instrumented through an allowlist while the same harness runs; the PHP runtime, the JSON output functions and the rest of libpg_query add no AFL++ tuples, and the full-harness maps equal the parse-only fuzz-target maps. Replay is per case.
coverage: Clang/LLVM source coverage of flow-php/pg-query-ext 0.48.0 ext/pg_query.c and source-built libpg_query 18.0.0 (bison/flex #line directives removed so lines map to the pinned gram.c and scan.c) during pg_query_parse() on a valid control; AFL++ feedback comes from the allowlisted ext/pg_query.c and libpg_query gram.c/scan.c/parser.c in the native overlay
parser_family: PostgreSQL grammar: libpg_query extracts the PostgreSQL 18 server raw parser (bison gram.c, flex scan.c, parser.c); shared with the C libpg_query path (18.1.0), pg_query_go, Rust pg_query, pglast and the libpg-query npm packages. The extension adds only the pg_query_parse() binding in ext/pg_query.c.
api: pg_query_parse(string $sql): string -> libpg_query JSON parse tree (RuntimeException on a parse error)
scope: SQL text from local bytes passed to the documented pg_query_parse(string $sql): string, which returns libpg_query's JSON parse tree; the harness json_decodes it and reads SelectStmt (targetList, JoinExpr, whereClause, groupClause, sortClause), InsertStmt (relation, cols, valuesLists), RangeVar, FuncCall and A_Const nodes, the same fields as the C libpg_query path. One statement per control.
observable_limits: The extension passes the PHP string to libpg_query as a C string, so text after an embedded NUL byte is not parsed. pg_query_parse_protobuf, fingerprint, normalize, split, scan, deparse, summary and PL/pgSQL functions are not exercised, nor are malformed input and the PG_QUERY_PARSE_* modes.
